findings.title: Incomplete or over-cap coverage can be bound and reserved before the 24-call allocation gate runs
evidence: runtime/delivery/utility_state.py:1124-1146 binds and reserves through _native_prerequisites without calling launch_allocation.
runtime/delivery/utility_state.py:375-390 validates the legacy plan and prerequisite gate, but not the supplemental runtime configuration or complete required_calls inventory.
runtime/delivery/utility_state.py:1212 calls utility_evidence.launch_allocation only after native-schedule-reserve has admitted an in-flight reservation.
runtime/delivery/utility_evidence.py:165-224 contains the required 24-call and exact-inventory checks.
tests/test_utility_native_lifecycle.py:171-178 deliberately binds and reserves a legacy planning plan, then expects rejection only at native_process_launch.
reproduction: Supply a native-plan/v1 that passes native_plan and a PASS native-prerequisites gate but has no versioned runtime_configuration or a call inventory that exceeds the cap.
Run native-schedule-bind and native-schedule-reserve; both reach their normal bind/reserve transitions because their path does not call launch_allocation.
Only native-process-launch rejects the allocation, after a durable reservation has already been consumed.
findings.impact: NI-01 requires missing coverage or more than 24 calls to prevent campaign admission. The current entrypoint admits and accounts a campaign attempt before enforcing the complete coverage oracle. This also conflicts with the lifecycle contract statement that schedule binding retains a complete frozen plan.
findings.expected_correction: Run launch_allocation during native-schedule-bind, retain and replay the allocation/runtime snapshots as part of the bound schedule identity, and reject reserve when that validation has not succeeded. Add a regression test proving that legacy, missing, and over-cap allocations cannot bind or reserve.
